issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 2.4(i), the matrix $G[f](x)$ is defined with $(1,2)$ entry $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ and $(2,1)$ entry $\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$. Because the conjugate transpose of $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ is $-\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)} \neq \overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$ whenever $\phi_2(f)(x) \neq 0$, $G[f](x)$ is not Hermitian, contradicting the explicit claim that it is Hermitian. Furthermore, the quadratic form identity in part (i) fails because the proof's derivation (line 351) produces $+\phi_2(f)(x)$ in the $(1,2)$ position, not $-\phi_2(f)(x)$. Consequently, the eigenvalues of $G[f](x)$ as defined do not equal $\check{f}(x)$ and $\hat{f}(x)$ (they can be non-real), invalidating part (ii). The same sign error propagates to Lemma 3.1 where $H_s = G[f_m]$ is also falsely asserted to be Hermitian.

failure_location.quote:
G[f](x):=\left[\begin{array}[c]{cc}
					\phi_1(f)(x)& -\phi_2(f)(x)\\
					&\\
					\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}&\phi_1(f)(-x)
				\end{array}\right]\in\mathbb{Q}_{(0,1)}^{2\times 2},\quad x\in[-\pi,\pi].

It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the $(1,2)$ entry of $G[f](x)$ in Definition/Theorem 2.4(i) and Lemma 3.1 from $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ to $\phi_2(f)(x)$, which restores Hermiticity and makes all subsequent derivations, Rayleigh quotient evaluations, and spectral identifications valid.
issues.overall_effect: The formal definition of the matrix symbol $G[f](x)$ in Theorem 2.4 is non-Hermitian and incompatible with the stated Rayleigh quotient integral and eigenvalue bounds in Theorem 2.4(i)-(iii), the Grenander-Szego theorem in Theorem 2.7, and the circulant spectrum characterization in Lemma 3.1.
issues.title: Erroneous sign in definition of symbol matrix renders it non-Hermitian and invalidates spectral claims
issues.why_classification: Replacing $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ with $\phi_2(f)(x)$ is a routine, local repair that matches the actual matrix derived in line 351 of the proof and preserves all stated theorems, bounds, and convergence results without needing any new proof architecture or weakening any result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagionalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices whereas general quaternion circulant matrices cannot be diagonalized by them.

Interestingly, the next lemma states that $c(T_n)$ can be diagonalized by $F_{\unitp,m}$ and its eigenvalues are the eigenvalues of 2-by-2 block matrices where their entries are the values evaluated at the partial sum of quaternion-valued generating functions.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims in the Abstract, Section 1, and Section 3.1 that Strang's circulant preconditioner $c(T_n)$ can be diagonalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices $F_{\unitp, n}$, unlike general quaternion circulant matrices. This is mathematically false: for any $c(T_n)$ where $\phi_2(T_n) \neq 0$, $F_{\unitp, n}^* c(T_n) F_{\unitp, n}$ is an X-shaped matrix with non-zero off-diagonal entries and cannot be diagonalized by $F_{\unitp, n}$. Lemma 3.1 and its proof only establish that the $2n \times 2n$ complex adjoint representation $\mathcal{M}(c(T_n))$ is unitarily block-diagonalizable into $2 \times 2$ diagonal blocks using $I_2 \otimes F_{\unitp, n}$.

failure_location.quote: We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagionalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices whereas general quaternion circulant matrices cannot be diagonalized by them.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the prose in the Abstract, Introduction, and Section 3.1 to state that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be block-diagonalized into $2 \times 2$ blocks by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices (or that their complex representations are block-diagonalized).
issues.overall_effect: The prose claims regarding the diagonalizability of Strang's circulant preconditioners by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices are false. However, the formal results rely only on the block-diagonal structure of the $2 \times 2$ representation.
issues.title: False claim that Strang's circulant preconditioners are diagonalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transforms
issues.why_classification: The error is entirely in the prose description of what is proved; correcting the statement from 'diagonalized' to 'block-diagonalized into 2-by-2 blocks' requires no changes to the algorithm or mathematical theorems.
